paragraphs.title: The Assembly of the People and the Holiness of the Sabbath

easy.question: Who gathered the entire assembly of the Israelites?
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel together.”

easy.question: On which day would the Israelites have a holy Sabbath of rest?
easy.explanation: The passage says, “on the seventh day there shall be to you an holy day, a sabbath of rest.”

easy.question: What was forbidden on the Sabbath?
easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.”

medium.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: Moses gathered the people and then delivered the Lord’s command
The people lit a fire and then listened to Moses
Moses scattered the people and then ordered them to work
medium.explanation: First Moses gathered the Israelites; afterward he told them what the Lord had commanded.

medium.question: In the phrase “throughout your habitations,” what does “habitations” mean?
answers: All the places where you live
All the days of your week
medium.explanation: “Habitations” means the places where people live, so the prohibition applied wherever the Israelites lived.

medium.question: What would happen to anyone who worked on the Sabbath?
answers: He would have to work more
He would be put to death
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly says that whoever worked on the Sabbath “shall be put to death.”

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “throughout your habitations”?
answers: The prohibition on kindling fire applied wherever people lived, not only in one place
The prohibition applied only in the tabernacle
The prohibition applied only in Moses’ house
challenge.explanation: “Throughout your habitations” extends the prohibition to all the places where the people lived.

challenge.question: What is the relationship between the general prohibition on work and the prohibition on kindling fire?
answers: Kindling fire was permitted, but other work was forbidden
Kindling fire was an explicitly mentioned example of work forbidden on the Sabbath
Kindling fire was permitted only during the six working days
challenge.explanation: Verse 2 forbids all work on the Sabbath, and verse 3 specifically adds that kindling fire was forbidden.

challenge.question: What major contrast is emphasized in verse 2?
answers: Between the six working days and the holy seventh day
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts the six days of work with the seventh day, a holy Sabbath of rest to the Lord.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “throughout your habitations”?
answers: The prohibition on kindling fire applied wherever people lived, not only in one place
The prohibition applied only in the tabernacle
The prohibition applied only in Moses’ house
questions.explanation: “Throughout your habitations” extends the prohibition to all the places where the people lived.

questions.question: What is the relationship between the general prohibition on work and the prohibition on kindling fire?
answers: Kindling fire was permitted, but other work was forbidden
Kindling fire was an explicitly mentioned example of work forbidden on the Sabbath
Kindling fire was permitted only during the six working days
questions.explanation: Verse 2 forbids all work on the Sabbath, and verse 3 specifically adds that kindling fire was forbidden.

questions.question: What major contrast is emphasized in verse 2?
answers: Between the six working days and the holy seventh day
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts the six days of work with the seventh day, a holy Sabbath of rest to the Lord.

easy.question: Who spoke to the entire assembly of the Israelites?
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Moses spake unto all the congregation of the children of Israel.”

easy.question: Which metals are listed among the offerings?
easy.explanation: Verse 5 lists “gold, and silver, and brass.”

easy.question: What was the oil mentioned in the passage used for?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And oil for the light.”

medium.question: What does “whosoever is of a willing heart” mean in this context?
answers: Anyone who wishes to give willingly
Anyone chosen for an official position
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a person who gives freely and willingly.

medium.question: Which combination correctly describes the uses mentioned in the passage?
answers: Oil for garments and spices for making wood
Oil for the light and spices for anointing oil and sweet incense
Stones for the light and wood for incense
medium.explanation: The passage distinguishes oil for the light from spices used for anointing oil and sweet incense.

medium.question: What is mentioned after the blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, and goats’ hair?
answers: Onyx stones and stones to be set
Rams’ skins, badgers’ skins, and shittim wood
medium.explanation: After listing the fabrics and goats’ hair, the next verse lists dyed rams’ skins, badgers’ skins, and shittim wood.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “Take ye from among you” and “a willing heart”?
answers: The Israelites gave their offerings willingly
Only Moses was allowed to give
The offering was taken forcibly from everyone
challenge.explanation: The phrases indicate that the people brought their offerings freely.

challenge.question: What exact distinction is made between the oil and the spices in verse 8?
answers: The oil was for anointing and the spices were for the light
The oil was for the light, while the spices were for anointing oil and incense
The oil was for the ephod and the spices for the breastplate
challenge.explanation: The verse assigns the oil to the light and the spices to anointing oil and sweet incense.

challenge.question: What were the onyx stones and the stones to be set intended for?
challenge.explanation: The passage says they were for “the ephod, and for the breastplate.”

questions.question: What can be inferred from “Take ye from among you” and “a willing heart”?
answers: The Israelites gave their offerings willingly
Only Moses was allowed to give
The offering was taken forcibly from everyone
questions.explanation: The phrases indicate that the people brought their offerings freely.

questions.question: What exact distinction is made between the oil and the spices in verse 8?
answers: The oil was for anointing and the spices were for the light
The oil was for the light, while the spices were for anointing oil and incense
The oil was for the ephod and the spices for the breastplate
questions.explanation: The verse assigns the oil to the light and the spices to anointing oil and sweet incense.

questions.question: What were the onyx stones and the stones to be set intended for?
questions.explanation: The passage says they were for “the ephod, and for the breastplate.”

paragraphs.title: The Skilled Workers Build the Tabernacle and Its Furnishings

easy.question: Who was invited to come and make all that the Lord commanded?
easy.explanation: The passage says, “every wise hearted among you shall come, and make all that the Lord hath commanded.”

easy.question: What was provided for the light of the candlestick?
easy.explanation: Verse 14 mentions “the oil for the light.”

easy.question: For whom were the holy garments mentioned at the end of the passage?
easy.explanation: The passage refers to the holy garments for Aaron and the garments of his sons to serve as priests.

medium.question: Which furnishing is mentioned after the candlestick and its oil?
medium.explanation: After the candlestick and the oil for its light, the passage mentions the incense altar.

medium.question: In the phrase “his brasen grate,” what does “grate” refer to?
medium.explanation: The grate was a bronze grid belonging to the altar of burnt offering.

medium.question: Why are the pins of the tabernacle and court, and their cords, mentioned?
answers: To stabilize and anchor the structures
medium.explanation: The pins and cords secured the tabernacle and court and helped keep them stable.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that staves are mentioned for the ark, table, and altars?
answers: They were meant to be carried from place to place
They were made entirely of fabric
They were used to store garments
challenge.explanation: The staves were used to carry the furnishings, showing that they were designed to be transported.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the repeated mention of a “hanging” at the tabernacle entrance and the court gate?
answers: The area was open on every side
Curtains marked and separated the entrances
The hanging was used to light the candlestick
challenge.explanation: A hanging was a curtain or partition that marked and separated an entrance.

challenge.question: What does the shift from the furnishings to Aaron’s and his sons’ garments show?
answers: The garments were part of the lighting equipment
Only Aaron took part in tabernacle service
Tabernacle service included both the people who served and the clothing suited to their roles
challenge.explanation: The passage ends with priestly garments for serving in the holy place, linking the service with its ministers and their garments.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that staves are mentioned for the ark, table, and altars?
answers: They were meant to be carried from place to place
They were made entirely of fabric
They were used to store garments
questions.explanation: The staves were used to carry the furnishings, showing that they were designed to be transported.

questions.question: What can be understood from the repeated mention of a “hanging” at the tabernacle entrance and the court gate?
answers: The area was open on every side
Curtains marked and separated the entrances
The hanging was used to light the candlestick
questions.explanation: A hanging was a curtain or partition that marked and separated an entrance.

questions.question: What does the shift from the furnishings to Aaron’s and his sons’ garments show?
answers: The garments were part of the lighting equipment
Only Aaron took part in tabernacle service
Tabernacle service included both the people who served and the clothing suited to their roles
questions.explanation: The passage ends with priestly garments for serving in the holy place, linking the service with its ministers and their garments.

easy.question: Who departed from Moses’ presence?
answers: The entire assembly of the Israelites
easy.explanation: The passage says, “all the congregation of the children of Israel departed from the presence of Moses.”

easy.question: What did the men and women bring for the Lord’s offering?
easy.explanation: The passage lists bracelets, earrings, rings, and other gold jewels.

easy.question: Which metals were brought as offerings to the Lord?
easy.explanation: The passage specifically mentions offerings of silver and brass.

medium.question: What caused the people to bring an offering for the work of the tabernacle?
medium.explanation: The people came because their hearts stirred them up and their spirits made them willing.

medium.question: What did the Israelites do after departing from Moses?
answers: They came to bring their offerings
medium.explanation: After leaving Moses, they came and brought materials and offerings for the tabernacle.

medium.question: In this context, what does “his spirit made willing” mean?
answers: His spirit moved him to give willingly
medium.explanation: The phrase means that a person was inwardly moved to participate freely.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that gold, fabrics, skins, metals, and shittim wood were brought?
answers: The offering included many different materials
challenge.explanation: The verses list a broad variety of materials rather than one single type.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “both men and women” show in this context?
answers: Men and women both participated in the offering
Women were forbidden to bring anything
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly describes men and women bringing offerings together.

challenge.question: What special detail appears in verse 24 about those who did not bring silver or brass?
answers: They did not participate at all
challenge.explanation: Anyone who had shittim wood for the work brought it.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that gold, fabrics, skins, metals, and shittim wood were brought?
answers: The offering included many different materials
questions.explanation: The verses list a broad variety of materials rather than one single type.

questions.question: What does the phrase “both men and women” show in this context?
answers: Men and women both participated in the offering
Women were forbidden to bring anything
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly describes men and women bringing offerings together.

questions.question: What special detail appears in verse 24 about those who did not bring silver or brass?
answers: They did not participate at all
questions.explanation: Anyone who had shittim wood for the work brought it.

easy.question: What did the wise-hearted women do with their hands?
easy.explanation: The passage says that they spun with their hands.

easy.question: What material did the women in verse 26 spin?
easy.explanation: Verse 26 specifically says that they spun goats’ hair.

easy.question: What colors and material did the women bring in verse 25?
answers: Blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen
easy.explanation: The verse lists blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.

medium.question: What was the connection between the women’s wisdom and their actions?
answers: Their wisdom enabled them to spin and prepare materials for the tabernacle
Their wisdom caused them to avoid tabernacle work
Their wisdom helped them choose the nation’s leaders
medium.explanation: The verses connect their wisdom with their ability to spin materials for the tabernacle.

medium.question: What can be learned from the mention of both wise-hearted women and women whose hearts stirred them?
answers: Some women had skill, while others participated willingly
The women worked only after being forced
medium.explanation: The verses emphasize both their abilities and their willingness to participate.

medium.question: In this context, what does “whose heart stirred them up” mean?
answers: Women who carried their hearts in their hands
Women whose hearts moved them to volunteer
Women who learned to carry heavy loads
medium.explanation: The context shows that their inner willingness moved them to take part in the work.

challenge.question: Why can the women’s work be considered a real contribution to building the tabernacle, even though they are not described as constructing it?
answers: They spun materials used in the tabernacle’s work
They replaced Moses as leaders of the people
They guarded the camp during construction
challenge.explanation: Their spinning supplied materials needed for the tabernacle’s curtains and garments.

challenge.question: What linguistic distinction appears between the women in verse 25 and those in verse 26?
answers: Verse 25 describes them bringing water, while verse 26 describes them bringing fire
Verse 25 emphasizes wisdom of heart, while verse 26 emphasizes hearts stirred to act
Verse 25 refers to men, while verse 26 refers to children
challenge.explanation: Verse 25 emphasizes wise-hearted women; verse 26 emphasizes women whose hearts moved them to participate.

challenge.question: Which broad conclusion best fits both verses?
answers: Only people with official positions could contribute
The tabernacle work used only expensive materials
A contribution could come both from practical skill and personal willingness
challenge.explanation: The verses show women contributing through skilled spinning and through their willingness to participate.

questions.question: Why can the women’s work be considered a real contribution to building the tabernacle, even though they are not described as constructing it?
answers: They spun materials used in the tabernacle’s work
They replaced Moses as leaders of the people
They guarded the camp during construction
questions.explanation: Their spinning supplied materials needed for the tabernacle’s curtains and garments.

questions.question: What linguistic distinction appears between the women in verse 25 and those in verse 26?
answers: Verse 25 describes them bringing water, while verse 26 describes them bringing fire
Verse 25 emphasizes wisdom of heart, while verse 26 emphasizes hearts stirred to act
Verse 25 refers to men, while verse 26 refers to children
questions.explanation: Verse 25 emphasizes wise-hearted women; verse 26 emphasizes women whose hearts moved them to participate.

questions.question: Which broad conclusion best fits both verses?
answers: Only people with official positions could contribute
The tabernacle work used only expensive materials
A contribution could come both from practical skill and personal willingness
questions.explanation: The verses show women contributing through skilled spinning and through their willingness to participate.

paragraphs.title: The Rulers Bring Stones and Oil

easy.question: Who brought the onyx stones and the stones to be set?
easy.explanation: The passage says, “the rulers brought onyx stones.”

easy.question: What were the onyx stones and the stones to be set intended for?
easy.explanation: The stones were brought for the ephod and the breastplate.

easy.question: What was brought for the light, anointing oil, and sweet incense?
easy.explanation: Verse 28 mentions spices and oil for these purposes.

medium.question: What order of events is described?
answers: First the stones were brought, and then the spices and oil
First the oil was brought, and then the stones
First the incense was brought, and then the spices
medium.explanation: Verse 27 describes the stones, and verse 28 continues with the spices and oil.

medium.question: For what purposes was the oil used?
answers: For the light and the anointing oil
For incense and the priests’ garments
medium.explanation: The oil was intended for the light and for the anointing oil.

medium.question: What does “the rulers” mean in this context?
medium.explanation: The rulers were leaders or heads of the tribes.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the division between the stones and the spices and oil?
answers: Each material had a particular role in tabernacle service
All the materials served the same purpose
The stones and oil were only decorations
challenge.explanation: The stones were for the ephod and breastplate, while the spices and oil served other sacred purposes.

challenge.question: What exact distinction is made between the oil and the spices?
answers: The oil was for garments and the spices for the light
The oil was for the light and anointing, while the spices were for incense
The oil was for the stones and the spices for the breastplate
challenge.explanation: The oil was used for the light and anointing; the spices were used for sweet incense.

challenge.question: Which pairing correctly matches a material with its use?
answers: Stones to be set — sweet incense
challenge.explanation: The passage connects the onyx stones with the ephod.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the division between the stones and the spices and oil?
answers: Each material had a particular role in tabernacle service
All the materials served the same purpose
The stones and oil were only decorations
questions.explanation: The stones were for the ephod and breastplate, while the spices and oil served other sacred purposes.

questions.question: What exact distinction is made between the oil and the spices?
answers: The oil was for garments and the spices for the light
The oil was for the light and anointing, while the spices were for incense
The oil was for the stones and the spices for the breastplate
questions.explanation: The oil was used for the light and anointing; the spices were used for sweet incense.

questions.question: Which pairing correctly matches a material with its use?
answers: Stones to be set — sweet incense
questions.explanation: The passage connects the onyx stones with the ephod.

paragraphs.title: The Willing Offering of All Israel

easy.question: Who brought the offering?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The children of Israel brought a willing offering unto the Lord.”

easy.question: Who participated in bringing the offering?
easy.explanation: The verse specifically mentions “every man and woman.”

easy.question: Why did the Israelites bring the offering?
answers: For all the work the Lord commanded
easy.explanation: They brought it for all the work the Lord had commanded Moses to arrange.

medium.question: What can be understood from “whose heart made them willing”?
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that their giving came from willing hearts.

medium.question: What happened after the Israelites became willing to give?
answers: They brought a willing offering to the Lord
medium.explanation: Their willingness was followed by bringing offerings for the tabernacle work.

medium.question: In the phrase “a willing offering,” what does “offering” mean?
medium.explanation: Here an offering is a gift or contribution given freely.

challenge.question: What special detail does the verse emphasize about those who participated?
challenge.explanation: The opening phrase “every man and woman” emphasizes that both participated.

challenge.question: What does “which the Lord had commanded to be made by the hand of Moses” show?
answers: Moses decided the work by himself
The Lord commanded it, and Moses conveyed the command
The Israelites did not know what to do
challenge.explanation: The phrase presents Moses as the one through whom the divine command was communicated.

challenge.question: What connection between willingness and the purpose of the offering appears in the verse?
answers: The gift was only meant to display wealth
The willingness had no connection to the work
Personal willingness was directed toward carrying out the Lord’s command
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the people’s willing hearts with bringing offerings for the commanded work.

questions.question: What special detail does the verse emphasize about those who participated?
questions.explanation: The opening phrase “every man and woman” emphasizes that both participated.

questions.question: What does “which the Lord had commanded to be made by the hand of Moses” show?
answers: Moses decided the work by himself
The Lord commanded it, and Moses conveyed the command
The Israelites did not know what to do
questions.explanation: The phrase presents Moses as the one through whom the divine command was communicated.

questions.question: What connection between willingness and the purpose of the offering appears in the verse?
answers: The gift was only meant to display wealth
The willingness had no connection to the work
Personal willingness was directed toward carrying out the Lord’s command
questions.explanation: The verse connects the people’s willing hearts with bringing offerings for the commanded work.

paragraphs.title: Bezalel Chosen for the Holy Work

easy.question: Who spoke these words to the Israelites?
easy.explanation: The verse begins, “And Moses said unto the children of Israel.”

easy.question: Whom did the Lord call by name?
easy.explanation: The Lord called Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, by name.

easy.question: To which tribe did Bezalel belong?
easy.explanation: The verse identifies him as belonging to the tribe of Judah.

medium.question: What can be understood from the Lord calling Bezalel by name?
answers: He was chosen for a special role
medium.explanation: Calling Bezalel by name shows that he was specifically selected for a particular task.

medium.question: In the phrase “called by name,” what does “called” mean?
medium.explanation: The context indicates a special personal summons or selection.

medium.question: What does the verse tell us about Bezalel’s family?
answers: He was the son of Uri, the son of Hur
He was the son of Moses, the son of Aaron
He was the son of Judah, the son of Jacob
medium.explanation: The verse gives his lineage as Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur.

challenge.question: Why is Bezalel’s tribe mentioned as well as his name?
answers: To identify his place of origin among Israel
To say that he was the tribe’s king
To show that he was not an Israelite
challenge.explanation: “Of the tribe of Judah” identifies his tribal affiliation within Israel.

challenge.question: What is the order of Bezalel’s lineage in the verse?
challenge.explanation: The verse names Bezalel first, followed by his father Uri and grandfather Hur.

challenge.question: What important difference is there between “called by name” and a general mention of a person?
answers: It emphasizes personal identification and selection
It says that Bezalel was unknown
It describes his place of residence
challenge.explanation: Calling him by name emphasizes that the Lord personally identified and chose him.

questions.question: Why is Bezalel’s tribe mentioned as well as his name?
answers: To identify his place of origin among Israel
To say that he was the tribe’s king
To show that he was not an Israelite
questions.explanation: “Of the tribe of Judah” identifies his tribal affiliation within Israel.

questions.question: What is the order of Bezalel’s lineage in the verse?
questions.explanation: The verse names Bezalel first, followed by his father Uri and grandfather Hur.

questions.question: What important difference is there between “called by name” and a general mention of a person?
answers: It emphasizes personal identification and selection
It says that Bezalel was unknown
It describes his place of residence
questions.explanation: Calling him by name emphasizes that the Lord personally identified and chose him.

paragraphs.title: The Spirit of God and Skilled Craftsmanship

easy.question: With what did the Spirit of God fill Bezalel?
answers: Wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and every kind of workmanship
easy.explanation: The passage says that God filled him with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and workmanship.

easy.question: With which materials did he know how to work?
easy.explanation: Verse 32 mentions his ability to work in gold, silver, and brass.

easy.question: What other materials did he work with?
easy.explanation: Verse 33 mentions cutting stones and carving wood.

medium.question: What is the connection between the Spirit of God and the craftsmanship described?
answers: The Spirit prevented him from working with materials
The Spirit gave him wisdom and skill for many kinds of work
The Spirit caused him to work only with wood
medium.explanation: The passage connects being filled with God’s Spirit to wisdom, understanding, and varied craftsmanship.

medium.question: In the phrase “in the cutting of stones, to set them,” what does “to set them” mean?
answers: To cut or decorate stones for setting
medium.explanation: The context describes cutting and setting stones, not counting or melting them.

medium.question: Which sequence correctly describes the ideas in the passage?
answers: Woodworking, then receiving wisdom, then working with gold
Stonework only, followed by stopping the work
Receiving wisdom and skill, working with metals, then working with stone and wood
medium.explanation: The passage first describes the source of his ability, then metalwork, followed by work in stone and wood.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “to devise curious works”?
answers: The work required only physical strength
He could plan and develop ideas for his work
He avoided working with different materials
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers not only to manual work but also to designing and planning.

challenge.question: What does the list of gold, silver, brass, stone, and wood show about his abilities?
answers: He could work with many materials and kinds of craftsmanship
He specialized in only one material
He only calculated the value of materials
challenge.explanation: The variety of materials indicates broad skill in several areas of craftsmanship.

challenge.question: What does “cunning work” mean in this context?
answers: Work whose purpose was only to think
challenge.explanation: The context presents craftsmanship requiring design, planning, and skill.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “to devise curious works”?
answers: The work required only physical strength
He could plan and develop ideas for his work
He avoided working with different materials
questions.explanation: The phrase refers not only to manual work but also to designing and planning.

questions.question: What does the list of gold, silver, brass, stone, and wood show about his abilities?
answers: He could work with many materials and kinds of craftsmanship
He specialized in only one material
He only calculated the value of materials
questions.explanation: The variety of materials indicates broad skill in several areas of craftsmanship.

questions.question: What does “cunning work” mean in this context?
answers: Work whose purpose was only to think
questions.explanation: The context presents craftsmanship requiring design, planning, and skill.

paragraphs.title: The Gift of Teaching to the Craftsmen

easy.question: What did the Lord put in the hearts of Bezalel and Aholiab?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord put it in their hearts to teach.

easy.question: Who was Aholiab?
answers: A man of the tribe of Judah
The son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan
easy.explanation: The verse identifies Aholiab as the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

easy.question: In this context, what does “put in his heart” mean?
answers: Gave him the ability and desire
easy.explanation: The phrase means that the Lord gave them both the ability and the desire to teach.

medium.question: What does “to teach” mean in the phrase “he hath put in his heart that he may teach”?
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the ability to teach and pass knowledge on to others.

medium.question: What can be learned from the fact that both Bezalel and Aholiab received the ability to teach?
answers: They could teach others their skills
They came from the same tribe
medium.explanation: The verse connects both men with the ability to teach their knowledge and craftsmanship.

medium.question: Why is Aholiab’s tribe mentioned?
answers: To say that he was a king
To describe where he lived in Egypt
medium.explanation: “Of the tribe of Dan” identifies Aholiab’s place among the tribes of Israel.

challenge.question: To whom does the pronoun “he” refer at the beginning of the verse?
challenge.explanation: The pronoun continues the previous subject, Bezalel, before Aholiab is introduced.

challenge.question: What is the main new point about Bezalel and Aholiab’s roles?
answers: They not only did the work but also taught it
They replaced Moses as leaders of the people
They worked only for the tribe of Dan
challenge.explanation: The verse adds teaching ability to their craftsmanship.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from mentioning Bezalel and Aholiab together even though they came from different tribes?
answers: Only members of one tribe could work on the tabernacle
Craftsmanship and teaching were given to people from different tribes
challenge.explanation: The two men came from different tribes, yet both were chosen and enabled to work and teach.

questions.question: To whom does the pronoun “he” refer at the beginning of the verse?
questions.explanation: The pronoun continues the previous subject, Bezalel, before Aholiab is introduced.

questions.question: What is the main new point about Bezalel and Aholiab’s roles?
answers: They not only did the work but also taught it
They replaced Moses as leaders of the people
They worked only for the tribe of Dan
questions.explanation: The verse adds teaching ability to their craftsmanship.

questions.question: What can be inferred from mentioning Bezalel and Aholiab together even though they came from different tribes?
answers: Only members of one tribe could work on the tabernacle
Craftsmanship and teaching were given to people from different tribes
questions.explanation: The two men came from different tribes, yet both were chosen and enabled to work and teach.

easy.question: With what did the Lord fill them?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Them hath he filled with wisdom of heart.”

easy.question: With which colors and materials did the embroiderers work?
answers: Blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen
easy.explanation: The verse mentions embroidery in blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen.

easy.question: What did the people described in the verse do?
answers: They performed crafts and devised designs
easy.explanation: The verse describes people who did every kind of work and devised skillful designs.

medium.question: What can be understood from their receiving wisdom of heart in order to work?
answers: They did not need to learn anything
Wisdom helped them perform their work skillfully
medium.explanation: The verse connects wisdom of heart with the ability to perform many kinds of work.

medium.question: In the phrase “the work of the engraver,” what does “engraver” mean?
medium.explanation: Here the word refers to a craftsman or artisan, not to someone who cannot hear.

medium.question: What relationship does the verse show between doing work and devising designs?
answers: They only thought and did not make anything
They both carried out the work and planned creative designs
medium.explanation: The verse presents both practical production and creative thought or planning.

challenge.question: What does “wisdom of heart” mean in this context?
challenge.explanation: Because the wisdom enabled craftsmanship, it refers to practical understanding and skill.

challenge.question: Which option most accurately describes the variety of activities in the verse?
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions engravers, craftsmen, embroiderers, weavers, and those who devise skillful work.

challenge.question: Which of the following is not mentioned as a material or color in the verse?
challenge.explanation: The verse mentions blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, but not gold.
